tabs.introductionDescription: Review size, valve, material, and model basics before opening the calculator.
tabs.calculatorDescription: Enter rim depth and pump-head parameters to review valve length, extenders, and effective exposure.

size.title: Choose Your Size
size.description: All necessary size information, such as ETRTO or inch size, can be found on your tire sidewall.

valves.introduction: Identify the valve shape first, then confirm compatibility from the rim hole's minimum effective diameter. The valve type, hole size, and tubeless seal must all match; tire size alone is not enough.
valves.imageOverviewAlt: Schwalbe inner tube valve types and lengths: Schrader, Dunlop, and Presta

av.description: Usually uses an approximately 8.5 mm hole. Common on mountain, commuter, and fat bikes, and also used by some tubeless systems; it works with a car-style pump head.
av.fit: Fit check: confirm that the rim explicitly supports a Schrader/AV hole; do not enlarge a hole or force a large valve into a Presta rim.

dv.description: A traditional valve found on city bikes and some European bicycles. Hole size and retaining hardware can vary by rim and valve version, so appearance alone is not enough.
dv.fit: Fit check: measure the rim hole and confirm the valve specification; do not apply the AV or SV measurement blindly.

sv.description: Usually uses an approximately 6 mm hole. Common on road bikes, gravel bikes, and many deep carbon rims; native lengths include 40, 50, 60, 80, and 100 mm.
sv.fit: Fit check: most road tubeless rims use Presta, but tubeless support does not automatically mean Presta; confirm the hole and rim instructions.

measure.title: How do I confirm which valve fits the rim?
measure.stepOne: Check the rim label, manual, or manufacturer specification for Presta/SV, Schrader/AV, or Dunlop/DV. For a tubeless rim, also confirm the valve-base and sealing profile.
measure.stepTwo: Remove the tire and tube, then measure the narrowest part of the rim hole with a caliper. Do not measure the outer countersink, chamfer, washer, or the outside of the valve base.
measure.stepThree: Compare the measured hole with the reference ranges below, then confirm the tube's valve-root shape and the rim maker's instructions. When the size is uncertain, keep the rim's original valve specification.
measure.warning: A hole that is too small can pinch the valve or stop it passing through; a hole that is too large lets the valve move and wear the tube root. Do not drill a carbon rim larger yourself. Use a reducer, washer, or grommet only when the manufacturer supports it.

holeReference.title: Rim valve-hole diameter reference

dv.diameter: Often close to 8.5 mm; confirm the exact specification

holeReference.note: These are common reference values, not a universal standard. Chamfers, washers, and the valve base can change the actual fit.

tubeless.title: Are tubeless-ready rims always Presta?
tubeless.description: No. Road and gravel tubeless rims commonly use Presta, while some mountain-bike, fat-bike, and other tubeless systems use Schrader. Check the rim-hole diameter, tubeless valve-base seal, and manufacturer instructions instead of relying on the words “tubeless-ready” alone.

materials.title: Choose the material route first
materials.description: Material changes air retention, weight, installation feel, and maintenance. After choosing a material, confirm the size, valve length, and rim compatibility.

butyl.title: Butyl
butyl.description: Stable air retention, durable construction, and straightforward cost and maintenance make it suitable for commuting, training, and most everyday wheels.
butyl.fit: Choose it when reliability and easy maintenance come first.

latex.title: Latex
latex.description: It can offer attractive rolling feel and weight, but usually needs more frequent inflation and careful installation to avoid pinching or twisting.
latex.fit: Choose it when you are comfortable with more frequent checks and maintenance.

tpu.title: TPU
tpu.description: Light weight and compact storage suit riders focused on low weight and a small spare. Follow the brand instructions for repair, valve roots, and locknuts.
tpu.fit: Choose it after confirming the exact model's installation, repair, and valve-accessory requirements.

advanced.title: Technician-level failure-proof knowledge
advanced.description: Two easy-to-miss assembly checks that directly affect valve-root life and reliable inflation on deep rims.

carbonValveHole.title: Carbon-rim burrs can cut a TPU valve neck
carbonValveHole.description: Many ultralight TPU tubes have walls around 0.3 mm, but the exact thickness depends on the model. An unfinished carbon-rim valve hole, a burr, or a loose metal stem can create a cut at the valve root during inflation and riding.
carbonValveHole.rule: Inspect the hole by sight and touch before fitting. Use a valve-hole washer or grommet that matches the rim maker's specification; never force a tube through a burr.

co2Seal.title: CO₂ inflation can shrink a poor extender seal
co2Seal.description: Rapid CO₂ expansion can cool the valve and seal sharply. An ordinary or poor-quality O-ring, or an improvised thread-tape seal, can harden, shrink, or leak during a rapid inflation.
co2Seal.rule: For an RVC extender, use an OEM seal explicitly rated for CO₂ and low temperature. If the specification allows FKM (fluoroelastomer), follow the seal and extender compatibility instructions; an FKM label alone is not a universal guarantee.

fitment.title: Rim Depth, Valve Length, and Extender Fitment
fitment.description: Estimate the valve passage depth from the nominal rim depth, then check the effective valve exposure from the tube and extender. The 6.5 mm offset and configurable pump-head grip thresholds are reference model parameters; confirm the exact rim, tube, and pump specifications before installation.
fitment.loading: Loading valve fitment results from the backend…
fitment.error: The valve fitment service is temporarily unavailable. Try again shortly.

visuals.description: The grey rim, dark native valve, and blue extender update with the rim depth and selection mode.

controls.rimDepthRange: Enter any whole number from {min}–{max} mm; the slider adjusts in 1 mm steps.
controls.measurementNote: Enter the rim maker's nominal rim depth, not the tire outside diameter. The selected ±{tolerance} mm is checked at both interval boundaries; confirm the exact rim section when the status changes across the range.
controls.pumpHeadGripDepthRange: How much valve stem the pump head needs to hold reliably: {min}–{max} mm.
controls.rimDepthUncertaintyRange: Review the same setup at nominal depth ± the selected value (0–{max} mm).

optimal.title: Comfortable exposure
optimal.description: The current total is {totalLength} with {clearance} of effective exposure. At {preferredExposure} mm or more, the pump head usually has a more stable grip.

marginal.title: Exposure is marginal
marginal.description: The current total is {totalLength} with {clearance} of effective exposure. It reaches the {gripDepth} mm grip-depth reference but leaves little margin; deep holes or another pump head may need more length.

unsafe.title: Exposure is too short
unsafe.description: The current total is {totalLength} with only {clearance} of effective exposure. Below {gripDepth} mm, do not force the pump head onto it; use a longer tube or a compatible extender.

metrics.passageFormula: Rim depth {rimDepth} mm − outer lip offset {offset} mm
metrics.automaticRecommendation: The reference combination is selected from the rim-depth range.
metrics.manualSelection: Manual combinations are for checking clearance and do not replace manufacturer specifications.

recommendationReasons.shortestNativeValveMeetsMinimum: The backend selected the shortest native valve that reaches the {minimumLength} mm minimum required total.
recommendationReasons.shortestExtenderAssemblyReachesMinimum: The native valve alone does not reach the {minimumLength} mm minimum required total, so the backend selected the shortest supported assembly that does.
recommendationReasons.manualCombination: This is a manual combination; the backend calculates its margins but does not treat it as an automatic recommendation.

uncertainty.title: Measurement-error interval review
uncertainty.description: The current assembly is rechecked from {lower} to {upper} mm of rim depth (nominal ±{uncertainty} mm).
uncertainty.stable: The status stays {status} across the selected measurement interval.
uncertainty.unstable: The status changes within the selected interval; use the worst case ({status}) and remeasure before installation.

alternatives.title: Compare usable assemblies
alternatives.description: These are backend-calculated reference assemblies for the current rim depth, not specific products. Click one to load it into manual fit checking.

matrix.title: Rim-depth and valve-exposure reference
matrix.description: Click a row to load its rim depth into the fit check above. Each cell shows the estimated effective exposure for that native valve length.

removableCore.label: Removable core
removableCore.title: Removable valve core (RVC)
removableCore.description: The core can be removed with the correct tool, allowing the original core to be moved to the outer end of an extender for normal inflation and pressure checks.
removableCore.rule: For a deep rim that may need an extender, prioritize a tube explicitly marked as having a removable valve core.

fixedCore.label: Fixed core
fixedCore.title: Fixed valve core
fixedCore.description: The core is riveted or formed as one piece with the valve stem and cannot be transferred using an RVC setup.
fixedCore.rule: Do not treat a generic sleeve extender as an RVC extender; confirm the tube and extender instructions first.

rvcExtender.label: RVC extender
rvcExtender.title: RVC extender assembly
rvcExtender.description: Remove the original core, install it at the top of the extender, and complete the seal and tightening steps specified by the product.
rvcExtender.rule: Calculate the extender together with rim depth and pump-head clearance instead of checking total length alone.

rootProtection.label: Root protection
rootProtection.title: Valve root and rim-hole protection
rootProtection.description: The tube root should sit naturally and the rim hole should be smooth. On carbon rims, use a protective or anti-rattle part only when the rim maker recommends it.
rootProtection.rule: Tighten the outer nut gently by hand; do not use pliers or pull the tube root tight.

shortValve.title: Valve exposure is too short
shortValve.description: When too little stem is exposed, the pump head may not pass the core neck reliably and can slip or bend the valve pin while inflating.
shortValve.rule: Target at least 15 mm; for deep rims, move to a longer native valve or use a compatible RVC extender.

overTightenedLocknut.title: Over-tightened locknut
overTightenedLocknut.description: Excessive tightening turns small movement between the rim hole and tube into tension at the tube root, increasing slow-leak and tearing risk.
overTightenedLocknut.rule: Turn the nut into place with two fingers and follow the tube maker's instructions.

fixedCoreExtender.title: Using an extender on a fixed core
fixedCoreExtender.description: A fixed-core tube usually cannot move its original core to the top of an RVC extender, which can cause pressure-reading errors or a leaking joint.
fixedCoreExtender.rule: Before buying for a deep rim, confirm the removable-core and extender compatibility.

carbonHole.title: Rough rim valve hole
carbonHole.description: Burrs or a loose metal stem in a carbon rim hole can create rattling and gradually wear the valve root.
carbonHole.rule: Inspect the hole and stem fit, then follow the rim maker's guidance for protective or anti-rattle parts.

fitment.disclaimer: This is a reference selection model based on the supplied board formula, not certification for a specific rim, tube, or pump model. Confirm tire size, rim-hole diameter, valve-core structure, maximum pressure, and manufacturer instructions before installation.

standard.title: Standard
standard.description: Reliable air retention, high-purity rubber, and uniform wall thickness.

airPlus.title: Air Plus
airPlus.description: Thicker walls hold air longer and provide better puncture protection.

extralight.title: Extralight / XXLight
extralight.description: Reduced weight for racing. Available in select sizes.

downhill.title: Downhill
downhill.description: Extremely robust, with a reinforced base and valve shear protection.
